items.q: Which hypothalamic nucleus is designated as the primary master pacemaker for circadian rhythms, receiving direct photic synchronization from retinal ganglion cells via the retinohypothalamic tract?
items.exp: The suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) of the anterior hypothalamus is the master circadian oscillator, synchronized to light-dark cycles by melanopsin retinal ganglion cells.
r: Correct. Suprachiasmatic nucleus generates circadian rhythms synchronized by retinal input.
Incorrect. Ventromedial nucleus governs satiety.
Incorrect. Lateral nucleus governs hunger.
Incorrect. Arcuate nucleus produces regulatory releasing hormones and dopamine.
items.kp: The suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) of the hypothalamus coordinates circadian rhythms via retinohypothalamic tract input.

items.q: Bilateral experimental destruction of the ventromedial hypothalamic nuclei in animal models produces which behavioral and metabolic consequence?
o: Hyperphagia, voracious appetite, and severe obesity
items.exp: The ventromedial nucleus is the satiety center (stimulated by leptin). Destruction eliminates satiety, causing persistent hyperphagia, savage rage, and rapid gross obesity.
r: Correct. Ventromedial destruction destroys the satiety center, causing uncontrolled hyperphagia and obesity.
Incorrect. Aphagia occurs with lateral hypothalamic destruction.
Incorrect. Adipsia occurs with preoptic thirst center lesions.
Incorrect. Hyperthermia occurs with anterior hypothalamic lesions.
items.kp: The ventromedial hypothalamic nucleus is the satiety center; destruction produces hyperphagia and profound obesity.

items.q: Bilateral destruction of the lateral hypothalamic area produces which phenotype?
o: Aphagia, cessation of feeding, and severe emaciation
items.exp: The lateral hypothalamic area is the hunger center (stimulated by ghrelin, inhibited by leptin). Destruction causes complete aphagia and starvation unless tube fed.
r: Correct. Lateral hypothalamic destruction causes aphagia and emaciation.
Incorrect. Hyperphagia occurs with ventromedial lesions.
Incorrect. Hyperthermia relates to anterior hypothalamic injury.
Incorrect. Narcolepsy relates to orexin/hypocretin neuron loss.
items.kp: The lateral hypothalamic area is the feeding center; bilateral destruction leads to complete aphagia and starvation.

items.q: Which hypothalamic nucleus is primarily responsible for detecting elevated core body temperature and orchestrating physiological heat dissipation via sweating and cutaneous vasodilation?
items.exp: The anterior hypothalamus (preoptic area) detects warm blood and coordinates heat loss responses (sweating, cutaneous vasodilation). 'A/C = Anterior Cools'.
r: Correct. Anterior hypothalamus detects elevated core temperature and triggers heat loss responses.
Incorrect. Posterior hypothalamus mediates heat generation (shivering).
Incorrect. Dorsomedial nucleus regulates GI motility.
Incorrect. Mammillary bodies process memory.
items.kp: The anterior hypothalamus acts as the heat dissipation center (cooling), while the posterior hypothalamus coordinates heat conservation.

items.q: Which neurohormones are synthesized within the cell bodies of the supraoptic and paraventricular hypothalamic nuclei and transported axonally to the posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis)?
items.exp: The supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei synthesize ADH and oxytocin, packaged with neurophysins and transported along the hypothalamo-hypophysial tract to Herring bodies in the neurohypophysis.
r: Correct. Supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei synthesize ADH and oxytocin.
Incorrect. GH and prolactin are synthesized in the anterior pituitary.
Incorrect. ACTH and TSH are anterior pituitary hormones.
Incorrect. LH and FSH are anterior pituitary gonadotropins.
items.kp: The supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei synthesize ADH and oxytocin for storage in the posterior pituitary.

items.q: In the sympathetic nervous system, what is the sole target organ where postganglionic sympathetic neurons release acetylcholine onto muscarinic receptors rather than norepinephrine?
items.exp: Almost all postganglionic sympathetic neurons release norepinephrine. The major exception is sympathetic innervation to thermoregulatory eccrine sweat glands, which is cholinergic (ACh onto M3).
r: Correct. Postganglionic sympathetic fibers to eccrine sweat glands release acetylcholine.
Incorrect. Pupillary dilator uses norepinephrine via alpha-1 receptors.
Incorrect. Ventricles receive norepinephrine via beta-1 receptors.
Incorrect. Renal vasculature uses dopamine and norepinephrine.
items.kp: Postganglionic sympathetic fibers innervating thermoregulatory eccrine sweat glands uniquely release acetylcholine onto muscarinic receptors.

items.q: A patient presents with unilateral miosis, mild ptosis, and facial anhidrosis (Horner syndrome). Instillation of 0.5% apraclonidine (alpha-2 agonist with weak alpha-1 activity) produces pupillary dilation and reversal of ptosis in the affected eye. Why does this occur?
o: Denervation supersensitivity of alpha-1 receptors on the pupillary dilator muscle
Release of stored norepinephrine from intact terminals
Direct stimulation of Edinger-Westphal parasympathetic output
items.exp: Sympathetic denervation leads to upregulation and hypersensitivity of post-junctional alpha-1 receptors on the dilator pupillae. Apraclonidine dilates the denervated pupil, confirming Horner syndrome.
r: Correct. Apraclonidine dilates the Horner pupil due to alpha-1 receptor denervation supersensitivity.
Incorrect. Apraclonidine does not block muscarinic receptors.
Incorrect. Cocaine tests for stored norepinephrine; apraclonidine acts directly.
Incorrect. Apraclonidine acts peripherally on iris smooth muscle.
items.kp: Apraclonidine reverses anisocoria in Horner syndrome due to denervation supersensitivity of pupillary alpha-1 receptors.

items.q: Which receptor subtype mediates parasympathetic bronchoconstriction and bronchial gland mucus hypersecretion in airways?
items.exp: Acetylcholine released from vagal parasympathetic postganglionic terminals binds muscarinic M3 receptors on bronchial smooth muscle (causing bronchoconstriction) and submucosal glands.
r: Correct. Muscarinic M3 receptors mediate bronchoconstriction and mucus secretion.
Incorrect. Beta-2 adrenergic receptors mediate bronchodilation.
Incorrect. Alpha-1 mediates vascular constriction.
Incorrect. Nicotinic receptors are in autonomic ganglia.
items.kp: Muscarinic M3 receptors mediate vagal parasympathetic airway bronchoconstriction and mucus secretion.

items.q: What is the primary action of sympathetic stimulation on the ciliary muscle of the human eye for distant vision?
o: Relaxation of ciliary muscle via beta-2 adrenergic receptors
Contraction of ciliary muscle via M3 receptors
items.exp: Sympathetic stimulation causes relaxation of the ciliary muscle via beta-2 receptors, flattening the lens for distant vision. Parasympathetic M3 stimulation contracts ciliary muscle for near accommodation.
r: Correct. Beta-2 sympathetic stimulation relaxes the ciliary muscle, flattening the lens for far vision.
Incorrect. Parasympathetic M3 stimulation contracts ciliary muscle for near accommodation.
Incorrect. Sphincter pupillae contraction is parasympathetic.
Incorrect. Retinal artery autoregulates.
items.kp: Sympathetic beta-2 stimulation relaxes the ciliary muscle to flatten the lens for distance vision.

items.q: Where are the preganglionic sympathetic cell bodies constituting the ciliospinal center of Budge located in the spinal cord?
o: Intermediolateral cell column of C8 to T2
Anterior motor horn of C3 to C5
Intermediolateral cell column of T10 to L2
Lateral horn of S2 to S4
items.exp: The ciliospinal center of Budge resides in the intermediolateral horn of C8 to T2 spinal segments, relaying descending hypothalamic sympathetic fibers to ascending preganglionics.
r: Correct. Ciliospinal center of Budge is located in the intermediolateral column of C8-T2.
Incorrect. C3-C5 anterior horn houses the phrenic motor nucleus.
Incorrect. T10-L2 provides lower visceral sympathetics.
Incorrect. S2-S4 provides parasympathetic outflow.
items.kp: The ciliospinal center of Budge in the C8-T2 intermediolateral column contains the second-order neurons for ocular sympathetic innervation.
